2026-11-08-shenzhen.html.title: Flexible Arrival Breakfast
2026-11-08-shenzhen.html.desc: Use the in-flight meal if timing works, or start gently with congee, buns and tea after landing. Keep this slot flexible around immigration and hotel check-in.

2026-11-08-shenzhen.html.title: Coconut Chicken · Futian
2026-11-08-shenzhen.html.desc: If arrival timing leaves room for lunch, coconut-chicken hotpot is a warm, easy first taste of Shenzhen without committing to a long cross-city outing.

2026-11-08-shenzhen.html.title: Shuiwei 1368 Food Street
2026-11-08-shenzhen.html.desc: Choose a low-pressure first-night food crawl near Futian: rice rolls, buns, skewers, desserts and tea, with enough variety for whatever jet lag allows.

2026-11-09-shenzhen.html.title: Fanlou Dim Sum · Huaqiangbei
2026-11-09-shenzhen.html.desc: Start beside the first shopping stop with shrimp dumplings, siu mai, congee and custard buns. Go early so breakfast does not eat into shopping time.

2026-11-09-shenzhen.html.title: Coconut Chicken · Huaqiangbei
2026-11-09-shenzhen.html.desc: Take a sit-down break without leaving the shopping zone. Coconut-chicken hotpot with claypot rice is a very Shenzhen lunch; choose a busy branch around Huaqiangbei.

2026-11-09-shenzhen.html.title: Dongmen Food Street
2026-11-09-shenzhen.html.desc: Finish where the shopping day already ends: skewers, dumplings, grilled seafood, sweets and drinks around Dongmen instead of another cross-city restaurant.

2026-11-10-shenzhen.html.title: Futian Dim Sum Breakfast
2026-11-10-shenzhen.html.desc: Have yum cha or congee near the hotel before MOCAPE. A fuller dim-sum breakfast works well because the rest of the morning is sightseeing.

2026-11-10-shenzhen.html.title: Nantou Ancient City Cafés & Snacks
2026-11-10-shenzhen.html.desc: Eat while exploring Nantou: cafés, bakeries, tea shops and small restaurants are mixed through the historic lanes, so lunch doubles as part of the visit.

2026-11-10-shenzhen.html.title: Happy Harbor Waterfront Dinner
2026-11-10-shenzhen.html.desc: Stay at Happy Harbor after Zhongshuge. Pick a photogenic café, casual Chinese restaurant or waterfront dinner spot, then walk the harbor before returning to Futian.

2026-11-11-guangzhou.html.title: Taotaoju Dim Sum · Tianhe
2026-11-11-guangzhou.html.desc: Make breakfast part of the Guangzhou day: classic Cantonese dim sum in the Tianhe shopping cluster, then continue straight into Taikoo Hui / Grandview.

2026-11-11-guangzhou.html.title: Taikoo Hui / Tianhe Lunch
2026-11-11-guangzhou.html.desc: Keep lunch inside the shopping district. Choose Teochew/Cantonese, noodles or another mall restaurant rather than losing an hour transferring elsewhere.

2026-11-11-guangzhou.html.title: Huifu Food Street · Beijing Road
2026-11-11-guangzhou.html.desc: Finish with a snack crawl near Beijing Road before the train back to Shenzhen: roast meats, dumplings, desserts and street-style snacks.

2026-11-12-guilin.html.title: Quick Breakfast before Shenzhen North
2026-11-12-guilin.html.desc: Keep transfer day simple: hotel breakfast or buns, congee and soy milk near the station instead of a special detour.

2026-11-12-guilin.html.title: Guilin Rice Noodles after Check-in
2026-11-12-guilin.html.desc: Your first Guilin meal should be mifen. Order a small bowl with braised toppings, peanuts and pickled vegetables near the hotel/lakes after dropping your bags.

2026-11-12-guilin.html.title: Zhengyang Night Food Street
2026-11-12-guilin.html.desc: After the Two Rivers & Four Lakes lights, walk into Zhengyang / the central pedestrian area for snacks, grilled food, desserts and local specialties.

2026-11-13-xingping.html.title: Guilin Rice Noodles before the Train
2026-11-13-xingping.html.desc: A fast bowl of mifen near the hotel is ideal before heading to the station for the short HSR ride toward Xingping.

2026-11-13-xingping.html.title: Xingping Beer Fish & Local Dishes
2026-11-13-xingping.html.desc: Eat inside Xingping Ancient Town so lunch does not interrupt the hanfu/photo route. Look for beer fish, stuffed river snails, bamboo chicken or Li River shrimp; ask the fish price before ordering.

2026-11-13-xingping.html.title: Light Dinner near Zhengyang / East-West Alley
2026-11-13-xingping.html.desc: You may still be full from beer fish, so keep the return-to-Guilin dinner flexible: noodles, dumplings, oil tea or snacks near the central lakes.

2026-11-14-guilin.html.title: Guilin Rice Noodles
2026-11-14-guilin.html.desc: Have another local mifen breakfast near the hotel before Elephant Trunk Hill; it is easy, local and inexpensive.

2026-11-14-guilin.html.title: Guangxi Lunch near Elephant Trunk Hill
2026-11-14-guilin.html.desc: Stay around Elephant Hill / the central lakes for lunch. Choose local Guangxi dishes such as taro, river fish, stir-fries or stuffed vegetables before the optional cave visit.

2026-11-14-guilin.html.title: Zhengyang Night Food Street
2026-11-14-guilin.html.desc: Use the relaxed evening for a proper snack crawl: grilled skewers, rice-noodle snacks, osmanthus sweets and whatever looked good on the first night.

2026-11-15-chongqing.html.title: Guilin Rice Noodles before Departure
2026-11-15-chongqing.html.desc: A quick mifen breakfast near the hotel is the easiest pre-train meal; save the heavier eating for Chongqing.

2026-11-15-chongqing.html.title: Chongqing Xiaomian · Jiefangbei
2026-11-15-chongqing.html.desc: After check-in, start with a bowl of Chongqing small noodles around Jiefangbei. It is fast, spicy and light enough to leave room for the evening food crawl.

2026-11-15-chongqing.html.title: Bayi Road Food Street
2026-11-15-chongqing.html.desc: Bayi Road is in the same Jiefangbei evening cluster as your skyline walk. Snack on suanlafen, chaoshou, skewers, crispy potatoes and ice jelly before or after Hongya Cave.

2026-11-16-chongqing.html.title: Chongqing Xiaomian
2026-11-16-chongqing.html.desc: Start with another noodle shop near Jiefangbei before Liziba. Choose mild/medium spice if you do not want to begin the day at full Chongqing heat.

2026-11-16-chongqing.html.title: Shibati Local Lunch
2026-11-16-chongqing.html.desc: Eat in the Shibati/Yuzhong cluster while you are already exploring the hillside streets: noodles, chaoshou, maocai or a simple local lunch all fit without a detour.

2026-11-16-chongqing.html.title: Chongqing Hotpot · Jiefangbei
2026-11-16-chongqing.html.desc: Make the full Chongqing day your hotpot night. Pick a busy restaurant around Jiefangbei, order a divided pot if useful, and finish with ice jelly or a cold dessert nearby.

2026-11-17-chengdu.html.title: Chongqing Xiaomian before the Train
2026-11-17-chengdu.html.desc: One last quick bowl near the hotel before the short rail hop to Chengdu keeps the morning efficient.

2026-11-17-chengdu.html.title: Chunxi Road Noodles & Buns
2026-11-17-chengdu.html.desc: After checking in, have a simple Chengdu lunch around Chunxi Road: noodles plus steamed buns/dumplings is ideal before the Taikoo Li shopping walk.

2026-11-17-chengdu.html.title: Taikoo Li Sichuan Dinner
2026-11-17-chengdu.html.desc: Stay in the Taikoo Li / Chunxi cluster for dinner. Choose a Sichuan restaurant for mapo tofu, twice-cooked pork, fish or lighter dishes, then continue the evening walk.

2026-11-18-chengdu.html.title: Early Chunxi Road Breakfast
2026-11-18-chengdu.html.desc: Eat early near the hotel before the Panda Base: noodles, buns, dumplings or hotel breakfast. The priority is reaching the pandas near opening time.

2026-11-18-chengdu.html.title: Wenshu Monastery Snack Crawl
2026-11-18-chengdu.html.desc: Lunch exactly where the afternoon itinerary lands: sweet-water noodles, liangfen, guokui and other Chengdu snacks around Wenshu. A vegetarian meal by the monastery is a calmer alternative.

2026-11-18-chengdu.html.title: Jianshe Road Night Market
2026-11-18-chengdu.html.desc: If you still have energy, make this the street-food night: grilled skewers, tofu, spicy noodles, duck-neck snacks, milk tea and brown-sugar ice jelly.

2026-11-19-chengdu.html.title: Chunxi Road Breakfast
2026-11-19-chengdu.html.desc: Keep breakfast near the hotel: noodles, buns, dumplings or soy milk before heading west toward People’s Park.

2026-11-19-chengdu.html.title: People’s Park Tea & Snacks
2026-11-19-chengdu.html.desc: Turn the teahouse stop into a light lunch. Tea plus dumplings, noodles or small Chengdu snacks keeps the afternoon comfortable before Kuanzhai Alleys.

2026-11-19-chengdu.html.title: Kuixinglou Food Street
2026-11-19-chengdu.html.desc: Walk from Kuanzhai toward Kuixinglou for a more food-focused dinner zone: skewers, Sichuan dishes, hotpot-style snacks and ice jelly before the opera.

2026-11-20-chengdu.html.title: Chunxi Road Breakfast
2026-11-20-chengdu.html.desc: A relaxed breakfast near the hotel fits the spa-day pace. Pick noodles/dumplings or a café breakfast depending how heavy you want lunch to be.

2026-11-20-chengdu.html.title: Spa-Day Light Lunch
2026-11-20-chengdu.html.desc: Keep lunch attached to the spa plan: use the spa restaurant/buffet only if your chosen venue actually includes food; otherwise eat a light meal near the hotel before going in.

2026-11-20-chengdu.html.title: Fuqin Night Market
2026-11-20-chengdu.html.desc: For a fun final night, graze through Fuqin: skewers, fried potatoes, grilled bites, cold noodles, ice jelly and sweets. Choose a sit-down dinner instead if you want a quieter finale.

2026-11-21-chengdu.html.title: Hotel / Chunxi Road Breakfast
2026-11-21-chengdu.html.desc: Have a dependable breakfast close to the hotel before the airport transfer. Avoid a destination breakfast that creates baggage or timing stress.

2026-11-21-chengdu.html.title: Airport Meal after Security
2026-11-21-chengdu.html.desc: Eat after check-in and security. If the ticket uses Tianfu (TFU), Terminal 1 has noodles, rice/soup options, coffee and fast food; verify your airport and terminal once the flight is booked.

2026-11-21-chengdu.html.title: In-flight / Connection Meal
2026-11-21-chengdu.html.desc: Plan dinner around the actual international itinerary. Use the airline meal if timing works, and buy water plus one good snack after security in case the connection is awkward.
